Refs: #3372

## Description

Chromium's V8 through at least 133, as shipped in the Android System
WebView, gives every Web IDL function own, frozen `arguments: null` and
`caller: null` properties. `lockdown()` could not delete them and threw,
so SES could not initialize there. `cauterizeProperty` now tolerates
exactly that shape with a warning, just as it already tolerates an
undeletable `prototype`. Any other value, or a writable pill, still
fails lockdown.

current `master`. #3372 also needed a `configstore`/`nconf` resolution
workaround for hardened-mode installs; `master` now carries an
equivalent fix, so that commit is no longer part of this change.

### Security Considerations

A frozen `null` is inert: it cannot change and it leaks nothing. Every
other undeletable shape still fails lockdown.

### Scaling Considerations

None.

### Documentation Considerations

The `ses` changeset describes the new tolerance.

### Testing Considerations

New tests plant pills on a replacement `Array.isArray` and check that a
frozen null pill passes lockdown with a warning, while a frozen non-null
pill and a writable null pill still fail. On the API 36 x86_64 emulator,
lockdown completes in the WebView with this change.

### Compatibility Considerations

`lockdown()` now succeeds on more inputs. It still fails on every shape
it failed on before, apart from the frozen null pill.
